title: Windcrest private linking & region gating intake
next_steps: Send private deployment network diagram and recommended CIDR plan
Share SOC2 + ISO27001 + KMS/BYOK security pack
Schedule hands-on pilot kickoff for week of Sep 13 (coordinate with Owen)
Provide rough pricing for Dedicated vs Private deployments (capacity tiers)
action_items: Ava Patel: Send network diagram and list of required IP ranges by Sep 6
Marco Jensen: Prep a short benchmark doc showing latency impact of peering vs privatelink by Sep 9
Lena Ortiz: Confirm target regions and data residency constraints by Sep 8
Owen Marsh: Share current Transit Gateway attachment counts and NAT architecture by Sep 7
summary: Discovery call to scope WindCrest's private/VPC onramp for Redwood Private. Covered VPC peering vs interface endpoints (Privatelink), Transit Gateway topology, egress IP and NAT concerns, region gating for EU-only data, authentication/KMS/SSO requirements, and pilot next steps.
topics: Egress IP stability and NAT/GW planning
Region gating and data residency (EU-only workloads)
questions: Can Redwood provision static egress IPs for outbound traffic?
How do you handle cross-account PrivateLink and endpoint owner flow?
What is the expected latency delta when routing over Privatelink vs peering?
Do you support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and HSM integration?
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-09-02 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Ava Patel (Redwood AE); Marco Jensen (Redwood SE); Derek Wu (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (WindCrest Head of Cloud); Tom Becker (WindCrest SRE); Priya Nair (WindCrest Security); Owen Marsh (WindCrest Network)

Summary: scoping Redwood Private/VPC onramp; network topology options, region gating, security controls, and pilot criteria.

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Ava from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Lena: Hi this is Lena, say hi, Head of Cloud at WindCrest.
[00:11] Tom: Tom here.
[00:13] Priya: Priya.
[00:14] Owen: Owen, network.
[00:16] Marco: Marco from Redwood, SE.
[00:18] Derek: Derek, solutions eng.
[00:20] Ava: Cool, thanks. The goal for today is to understand your networking posture and constraints so we can recommend Private vs Dedicated, and call out any edge cases for region gating.

[00:35] Lena: Yeah our primary ask is EU-only processing for a subset of models and we need audit logs and BYOK. We also want low latency for user facing inference in EU.
[00:47] Ava: Got it. So two constraints: region residency for data and KMS. We'll dig into how you currently isolate traffic.

[01:05] Owen: We run most infra in AWS in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. Transit Gateway hub with multiple accounts attached. We prefer interface endpoints over peering when cross-account because of route table scale, but open to tradeoffs.
[01:25] Marco: Right, and to be clear with Redwood Private we can do either VPC peering, Transit Gateway attachments, or AWS Interface Endpoints (Privatelink style) depending on what you want. Each has tradeoffs: peering is simple but scales poorly across lots of accounts, privatelink gives you stable endpoints and works cross-account but adds a hop and can add a few ms of latency.

[01:56] Tom: A few milliseconds is fine but we need predictable p95 under 150ms for our UI flows.
[02:03] Derek: If you're seeing 150ms end-to-end, what's your baseline today?
[02:09] Tom: Baseline is usually 60-80ms to our existing model endpoints in region.

[02:16] Marco: Okay, so the expectation would be adding Redwood Private with privatelink might add 5-12ms depending on region and cross-AZ hops. Peering often is slightly lower but then you need to manage route tables and IPs.

[02:34] Priya: Security question — do you support customer-managed KMS keys? We cannot have Redwood manage keys for the EU datasets.
[02:41] Ava: Yes, we support BYOK in Private — you can bring your KMS and we can integrate via encrypted flows. For HSM-level integration we have options via partner HSMs; we'll share a security pack.

[02:58] Priya: Great. Also SOC2, ISO — do you have up-to-date certs and audit log support? We need retention for 12 months at least.
[03:06] Derek: We have SOC2 and ISO3 — actually ISO27001. Audit logs are configurable; for Private we can stream audit logs into your S3 or to your SIEM via Kinesis or direct syslog. Retention can be tuned on your side.

[03:26] Owen: How do you secure egress? We need stable outbound IPs for allowlisting to partner APIs.
[03:33] Marco: For Private we can provide a small pool of static egress IPs per deployment region; commonly we put a NAT GW or egress gateway in your VPC controlled by you and you can reserve Elastic IPs. We also offer managed egress with static IPs if needed as an add-on.

[03:53] Lena: So if we use a Transit Gateway and attach Redwood, do we need to open any specific ports or is it just HTTPS outbound?
[04:01] Ava: All control plane comms happen over HTTPS 443. For data plane inference, traffic is internal once the endpoints are provisioned — but you will need to permit port ranges for interface endpoints if using privatelink; typically TCP 443 for the interface ENIs. Peering doesn't require anything special besides routing.

[04:22] Owen: Do you support cross-account privatelink where Redwood is the service provider? How are permissions handled?
[04:29] Marco: Yes, Redwood can be the endpoint service owner. The usual flow: you create an interface endpoint in your account to the service name we provide and accept the connection. For cross-account we exchange the endpoint service name and you attach. We typically send Terraform snippets to make this smoother.

[04:47] Tom: On quotas — we have high throughput spikes, are bursting and autoscaling supported? If we push a spike of 2x QPS, will Redwood spin capacity?
[04:56] Ava: For Private we provision a baseline and we can enable burst capacity; it depends on the plan. Dedicated has stronger SLA for throughput. We can propose a pilot cluster sized for typical + 2x burst and add autoscaling policies.

[05:15] Lena: Cost is a concern. How different is Dedicated vs Private?
[05:19] Derek: Dedicated is basically reserved GPU capacity in Redwood's hosted infra; Private is deployed in your VPC with an ops plane that can be customer-managed. Private tends to have higher setup and operational overhead but gives you data residency and KMS control. We will include pricing guidance in the follow up.

[05:40] Marco: A tip on topology: for EU-only gating we normally recommend putting inference nodes in eu-west-1 and creating privatelink interfaces in your EU accounts and routing egress through your EU NAT to ensure no data leaves region. If you need multi-region failover, we can replicate endpoints in eu-central-1 and failover with smart routing.

[06:05] Priya: About audit logs — are prompts and request payloads logged? We need to redact PII and also control retention.
[06:12] Ava: By default we log metadata and identifiers; you can configure whether full request/response bodies are logged in your auditing stream. For regulated data we recommend routing raw payloads to your S3 with server-side encryption and lifecycle rules for retention.

[06:30] Owen: IP planning — do you have recommended CIDR ranges for the Redwood side? We have a limited /16 we can spare but prefer predictable allocation.
[06:39] Marco: We'll propose a recommended plan. For interface endpoints you only need ENI IPs per AZ. For peering or TGW attachments we recommend reserving /24s per subnet cluster. We'll send a suggested CIDR map.

[06:56] Lena: Can we do an initial pilot for a single model group and validate latency and egress? Our timeline: POC in Sept, production by Nov if all goes well.
[07:05] Ava: That sounds doable. We'll aim for a pilot kickoff week of Sep 13 which gives us time to share docs and for you to lock regions.

[07:18] Tom: What's involved from our side to spin up privatelink? Who does the endpoint creation?
[07:23] Marco: We can provide Terraform modules and step-by-step guides; your network or infra team will create the interface endpoints and accept our service; we can also assist via a runbook session.

[07:35] Owen: Transit Gateway attachments — if we attach via TGW do you need AWS account access?
[07:40] Derek: No, we don't need access. We'll provision our side service and you attach. For TGW peering we exchange the TGW ID and attachments; it can be cross-account but works best when your team does the attach.

[07:55] Priya: SSO and RBAC — can Redwood map to our SAML provider and sync groups?
[07:59] Ava: Yes, SAML SSO is supported for the control plane (Console/Console access). For model level RBAC we integrate with SCIM and group sync; we'll share the SAML/SCIM docs.

[08:15] Marco: One network caveat — if you use privatelink and we host model shards in multiple AZs, your interface endpoints should be in each AZ for low latency; else cross-AZ traffic can add latency and cross-AZ charges.

[08:34] Tom: Are any ports opened to the public internet for health checks?
[08:38] Marco: Health checks are internal. For hosted we may need some outbound connectivity for updates, but in Private everything is internal to your VPC unless you opt-in for external monitoring; again, we can route telemetry through your log pipeline.

[08:53] Lena: For EU-only, will the control plane data (config, rollouts) ever leave the EU?
[08:58] Ava: We offer a customer-controlled private control plane option for Private deployments so you can keep control plane metadata in-region. If you choose Redwood-hosted control plane, we can sign contracts about data handling but the safest is a private control plane.

[09:15] Owen: What about egress to third-party APIs in the US? Some model augmentations call US-based features — if EU workload must not leave region, how do you handle external integrations?
[09:25] Derek: You can opt to disable outbound calls from EU nodes; for integrations that must hit US endpoints you'd need a separate workflow or a controlled proxy that you manage with allowlists. We can also run a paired US Private deployment and route specific calls there, but that creates cross-region flows that you must authorize.

[09:46] Priya: Encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between our VPC and the Redwood data plane?
[09:52] Marco: We can support mTLS for private deployments; we usually use TLS mutual auth for sensitive customers, certificates can be provided by you.

[10:01] Ava: To make sure we capture success criteria — Lena, can you list the must-haves?
[10:06] Lena: Sure. EU-only compute (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1), BYOK for KMS, audit logs streamed to our S3 with 12mo retention, static egress IPs, P95 latency under 150ms, and ability to scale for bursts to 2x baseline.

[10:24] Ava: Great. We'll map those to pilot acceptance.

[10:30] Marco: A few clarifying questions on the Transit Gateway counts — Owen, do you have any attachment limits or IP reuse constraints?
[10:36] Owen: We currently have 18 TGW attachments and we are close to our limit in the consolidation account. Adding more peering attachments is unpleasant. That's why we lean to privatelink for cross-account.

[10:49] Marco: Understood, privatelink is likely better given TGW scale limits. We'll call out the per-AZ ENI requirements.

[11:00] Tom: Any issues if we use a single shared VPC for dev and a separate one for prod?
[11:06] Derek: That's fine; we recommend separate deployments per environment to avoid noisy neighbor and to have clean access controls. Each environment can have its own endpoints and audit streams.

[11:18] Lena: On the BYOK flow, do you support key rotation and can Redwood access exposures if you rotate keys?
[11:25] Marco: You manage the keys; Redwood requests temporary decrypt via KMS but cannot extract keys. Rotation is supported; we'll coordinate a short maintenance window with you for key rollovers if needed.

[11:38] Priya: Regarding compliance, can you provide evidence for encryption at rest and separation of metadata for EU data?
[11:45] Derek: Yes, our security pack contains diagrams and controls; we'll send a subset marked for EU controls. We have customers in banking and have done similar attestations.

[11:58] Owen: Network egress cost — if traffic is internal in-region it's cheap, but cross-region transfer is expensive. If we plan multi-region standby, we need to budget cross-region costs.

[12:08] Marco: Yep, important callout. We'll include an estimate for cross-region replication and peak token throughput to help you model costs.

[12:20] Ava: Can we talk briefly about troubleshooting—if we see elevated latencies who do we call?
[12:25] Derek: For pilot we'll provide an SRE runbook and a single point of contact at Redwood for triage. For Dedicated/Private we offer enhanced SLAs with phone escalation.

[12:38] Tom: Do you offer tracing hooks for requests? We want correlation IDs to track user requests through our stack.
[12:44] Marco: Yes, Redwood supports tracing headers and will propagate X-Request-ID and can emit traces to your tracing backend or to our tracing collector; again configurable.

[12:55] Ava: Okay next, let's capture the actual steps to get pilot going — we'll need region selection, list of subnets, and who on your side will create endpoints.

[13:06] Lena: Owen will do the endpoint creation. I'll confirm regions — leaning eu-west-1 for pilot.
[13:11] Owen: Yep I can do that. I'll also share TGW attachments counts.

[13:17] Marco: We'll follow up with a short network checklist: CIDR suggestions, sample Terraform, security controls, and a latency bench doc.

[13:27] Priya: Can you include instructions for redaction of logs and PII handling?
[13:30] Derek: Absolutely, we'll include recommended redaction patterns and a mapping for which fields you might want to redact pre-ingest.

[13:40] Speaker 2: (unlabeled voice) also, you might want to--
[13:44] Tom: That's probably Owen.

[13:46] Marco: Noted. On the benchmarking piece: for Privatelink we typically see a 3-10% token processing latency increase vs local peering. For shorter response times that can still be a few ms. We'll quantify in the doc.

[14:03] Lena: Are there any constraints for private endpoints in GCP if we ever expand?
[14:07] Marco: GCP has VPC peering limits too and their equivalent interface endpoints exist; it's slightly different but we do private connectivity patterns for GCP as well. We'll note GCP caveats if you decide to multi-cloud later.

[14:21] Owen: Regarding CIDR, do you require non-overlapping ranges? We have some legacy overlaps with partner accounts.

[14:26] Derek: Yes, non-overlapping is required for peering/TGW-attach. For privatelink interface endpoints you avoid that requirement because ENIs are in your VPC and you don't route via peering. If you have overlapping IP space, privatelink is a safer option.

[14:42] Tom: On the security side, we want to run an internal pen test after pilot. Does Redwood support penetration testing of the Private deployment?

[14:50] Ava: Yes, with coordination and a test window. We have a pen test policy to ensure safe test scopes. We'll share the policy.

[15:00] Lena: Logistics — who should we loop for contract and pricing?
[15:04] Ava: I'll loop in Sales Ops and Solutions Pricing after the network doc; expected timelines for a commercial quote in a week once we size capacity.

[15:12] Owen: For the static egress IPs, what's the minimum pool? We prefer two for HA.

[15:17] Marco: Two is typical for HA, reserve at least two Elastic IPs per region. If you want provider-managed egress we can provide a small block, we'll include options.

[15:29] Priya: Any third-party audits or references in finance you can point to?

[15:33] Derek: We'll send a short references pack of other financial customers and redacted architecture diagrams.

[15:40] Ava: Great — we're running toward time. Quick recap and next steps?

[15:45] Lena: Recap: Pilot in eu-west-1, privatelink preferred, BYOK/KMS in region, audit logs to S3 12mo, static egress IPs, p95 < 150ms, burst 2x.

[15:58] Ava: Yes. Action items we recorded — we'll send the network checklist and terraform snippets and schedule the pilot kickoff week of Sep 13.

[16:06] Tom: Sounds good.

[16:08] Owen: I'll share TGW counts and existing CIDR ranges by Sep 7.

[16:12] Priya: I'll review the security pack and confirm BYOK details.

[16:18] Ava: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in an email with attachments.

[16:22] Marco: Thanks, talk soon.

End of recording.

Notes: transcript has some small attribution errors near 13:40 (unlabeled voice) and occasional filler words; all major action items enumerated above.
